column1: # Norwegian Bokmål (nb) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#            @plural              `source` is "one|other" (English forms); the translation lists the
#                                 language's forms separated by "|" (see `plural` in i18n.rs)
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Combined from the community Norwegian Bokmål catalogs in #8072 and #9025: each row takes the best
# of their translations, with one term per concept across the UI (lag, utvalg, maske, gradient,
# myk kant, transformer, rutenett, hjelpelinje, tegneflate, lerret, klippemaske, arbeidsområde,
# pensel, justering, kanal, bane, historikk, alternativer, forvalg, strek, sløring, hurtigtaster …).
# Clean-room: written from the plain meaning of the English labels; no proprietary localisation
# resource was consulted or copied. Labels use sentence case, commands are imperatives and the
# user is addressed as "du". Product, format and technology names (PhotoCraft, ArtCraft, OpenType,
# CMYK, Lab …) and key caps keep their spelling; the trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept.
# Decimal commas and a space before % follow Norwegian typography. Plural rule: one|other
# (n != 1 -> other); nouns like "lag" (layer) have the same form in singular and plural.
# Native-speaker review of the remaining specialist terms is welcome.
